references.text: Parallel regulation concerning the daily burnt offering with one lamb in the morning and one lamb at twilight
Repeats the instruction regarding the second lamb to be offered at twilight (בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם)
Elijah offers sacrifice at the time of the evening offering, pointing to the daily sacrificial practice
Reference to the evening offering (מִנְחָה) as the appointed time for prayer and sacrifice
Ezra prays at the time of the evening offering, demonstrating continuity in the daily sacrificial practice
Gabriel comes to Daniel at the time of the evening offering (מִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב)
Ezekiel's vision of the restored temple includes a daily morning offering with a lamb
The daily offering is contrasted with Christ's single, perfect sacrifice
The Lamb slain from the foundation of the world was laid down - Christ as the fulfillment of the sacrificial lamb
This is the direct legal parallel that confirms and establishes the order for the continual morning and evening offerings.
Confirms continuity in the sacrificial system by showing that the daily morning offering is a central part of the prophetic temple order.
Places other sacrifices in relation to the continual morning offering, confirming its role as the foundation of temple worship.
